title: POC weekly security sync - Sunrise Credit
summary: Weekly pilot security sync. Customer ran initial integration tests; SSO/SAML handshake partially successful, SCIM user provisioning pending. Discussed audit log export, retention windows, encryption/KMS, and SOC 2 artifacts. Agreed next steps: provide SOC2 whitepaper, sample audit logs, SAML metadata, and schedule a technical deep dive for SIEM ingestion with Marcus.
action_items: Maya Chen - send SOC 2 Type II report and security whitepaper (due 2026-08-07)
Ravi Patel - provide sample audit log export (anonymized) and event schema (due 2026-08-10)
Marcus Diaz - share SIEM (Splunk) ingestion endpoint and sample index names (due 2026-08-07)
Priya Singh - confirm required retention window and legal hold requirements (due 2026-08-12)
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and encryption architecture docs
Customer to complete SAML test with staging metadata
Schedule SIEM ingestion deep-dive (30-45m) with Marcus and Ravi
Agree final retention policy for pilot data (logs and prompts)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-05 14:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Ravi Patel - Redwood; Laura Kim, Marcus Diaz, Priya Singh, Owen Lee - Sunrise Credit

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um today is our weekly security sync for the pilot, high level we'll go through the s s o updates, audit logs, k m s questions and any blockers, and then next steps.
00:22 Laura Kim: hi thanks, appreciate it. we ran the SAML handshake yesterday, we saw a partial success, we got a login but the groups didn't come through.
00:31 Ravi Patel: ok that sounds like SCIM provisioning, sometimes group claims are mapped differently between IdPs. which identity provider are you using?
00:40 Laura Kim: we're on Okta, latest enterprise plan, and we pushed the metadata, we used the redwood staging metadata that you shared.
00:49 Ravi Patel: great, yeah for Okta we sometimes need the group claim in the assertion or SCIM for full group mapping, we'll send a recommended mapping. also check the audience and recipient fields, a couple customers have hit that.
01:06 Marcus Diaz: curious - we tried to pull audit logs from the pilot but the format looked a bit different than our SIEM expects. can you confirm the event schema?
01:15 Ravi Patel: sure, we can provide an anonymized sample export and a small schema doc. logs include request id, model, route, token counts, and user id hash, timestamps, region, and outcome codes. we mask full prompt content in the sample for PII concerns.
01:35 Owen Lee: are you able to stream logs to a syslog or do you support push to splunk HTTP event collector?
01:42 Maya Chen: we support S3 export, syslog via collector (we can set up a forwarder), and direct post to Splunk HEC in some configurations. for the pilot we usually do S3 drops or HEC.
01:57 Priya Singh: what's your default retention for audit logs during the pilot? our compliance wants 12 months for key events but we may keep the rest shorter.
02:06 Ravi Patel: default staging retention is 30 days but we can extend to 90 days on request; for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers retention is configurable and we can set up long term export to your S3 or customer storage for the full 12 months.
02:24 Laura Kim: ok can you confirm deletion workflows? if we ask to delete pilot data, how soon does it get purged?
02:31 Maya Chen: deletion is initiated within 48 hours and then background jobs scrub payloads; logs replicated to S3 will need manual trigger to clear depending on your bucket lifecycle. we'll include instructions in the doc we send.
02:47 Marcus Diaz: encryption questions: are keys customer-managed? we need to see support for KMS/bring-your-own-key and key rotation policies.
02:55 Ravi Patel: in Redwood Private we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK) and HSM integrations for on-prem. For hosted pilot, we can show envelope encryption with a customer key in some pilots; full BYOK needs dedicated/private mode typically.
03:12 Priya Singh: SOC 2 - do you have a current Type II and can we get the bridge letter or SOC report?
03:19 Maya Chen: yes we have a SOC 2 Type II for the last audit cycle; we'll share the report and our security whitepaper. some redactions are standard.
03:26 Laura Kim: perfect, also curious about access controls - can we do RBAC down to route-level and integrate with our SSO groups?
03:34 Ravi Patel: yes RBAC with role mappings is supported, you can map Okta groups to roles in Redwood, and we can scope tokens to specific routes. we'll send a sample policy mapping.
03:46 Owen Lee: any known limitations around KV cache or model state? we need to ensure no leakage across tenants in multi-tenant hosted setup.
03:54 Ravi Patel: multitenancy isolation is enforced at request routing and memory segmentation; KV cache is per-tenant and not shared. we'll include an architecture diagram that highlights isolation primitives.
04:05 Laura Kim: another ask - audit log granularity: do you log parameter-level changes, model version rollouts, who triggered deployments?
04:14 Maya Chen: yes actions like deployments, rollouts, model pin changes, and who/when (actor) are logged. we also keep route-level latency and error traces for debugging.
04:27 Marcus Diaz: for SIEM ingestion, can we get a sample HEC payload?
04:32 Ravi Patel: yes we'll provide that, plus a script to transform to your Splunk index.
04:40 Priya Singh: legal wants clarity on data residency for prompt data, are prompts stored outside region?
04:48 Maya Chen: for hosted pilot we keep data in the region you selected; we can pin region to US-West or EU-W depending on contract. prompt caching and KV caching are stored in that region and we have export controls.
04:59 Laura Kim: great. timeline: we need SOC2 docs by next week and the SAML mapping fixed so we can do a smoke test.
05:07 Maya Chen: noted - we'll send SOC2 and sample logs by Friday, and Ravi will follow up on the Okta mapping. schedule wise we'll get the SIEM deep-dive for next week as well.
05:18 Owen Lee: one last question - are you able to apply lawyer-provided data retention holds for eDiscovery?
05:25 Maya Chen: yes for enterprise customers we support legal hold operations and can export immutable archives to your storage, we'll outline the process.
05:33 Laura Kim: ok thanks everyone, that answers our blockers.
05:36 Maya Chen: thanks all, recap of action items and I'll drop the links in the follow-up.
05:40 Meeting end.
